summary: Full E2E testing of Delquro Connect backend (35 pytest cases across auth, huddle, timeoff, schedules, uploads, chat, kudos, achievements, admin/roles/locations, invites) and frontend (login, huddle, timeoff, schedule, chat, more page RBAC for admin vs staff). Backend 34/35 pass. Frontend flows fully working; RBAC gating correct.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout is ineffective behind the ingress. The identifier is built as `f"{request.client.host}:{email}"`, but in this k8s environment request.client.host is the pod-level proxy IP which alternates between multiple values (observed 10.232.132.143 and 10.232.131.130 in db.login_attempts). Result: attempts get split across identifiers and the 5-fail threshold is never reached for a real attacker. 6 wrong logins in a row returned 401 every time (never 429). Fix: key the counter on the normalized email alone (or extract X-Forwarded-For first hop) and cap total fails per email.

issues: AppLayout uses label.toLowerCase().replace(' ', '-') which yields 'nav-time-off', not the 'nav-timeoff' documented in the task/agent context. Same for tab-time-off. Not a functional bug, but the documented testid list is out of sync with the code. Suggest either updating docs or generating a canonical slug (e.g. replace(/\s+/g,'') for 'timeoff').

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout keying so that a single email/user across multiple proxy IPs is still locked out after 5 failed attempts (or use X-Forwarded-For / just the email).
Reconcile documented data-testid names ('nav-timeoff','tab-timeoff') with actual generated names ('nav-time-off','tab-time-off') — update either docs or AppLayout slug logic.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1035 lines — consider splitting into routers (auth, huddle, timeoff, chat, admin, files) as it grows.

CORSMiddleware is registered AFTER app.include_router(api). Starlette applies middleware to all routes regardless of order, but the more idiomatic (and safer with future middleware) pattern is to add middleware before including routers.
/api/files/{fid}: token is validated but there is no per-file ACL — any authenticated user can fetch any file id (uploaded schedules, chat images, avatars). Acceptable for MVP but worth noting.
Chat `access` field is stored but never enforced (only membership + is_everyone are checked). If 'staff/manager/admin' access tiers are intended, they are effectively dead config today.
PUT /api/team/{uid}/role and /api/team/{uid}/location take the role/location as query params rather than JSON body — works, but is non-idiomatic REST.
login_attempts entries are never TTL-expired; recommend a Mongo TTL index on locked_until or a periodic cleanup.

Only failing test is TestAuth.test_brute_force_lockout — see rca. Frontend nav testids in code are 'nav-huddle','nav-time-off','nav-schedule','nav-chat','nav-more' (note the hyphen in time-off).
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout bug — login() computes `identifier = f'{request.client.host}:{email}'` and `check_lockout` reads counters keyed on that identifier. Inside the emergent k8s ingress, `request.client.host` is the reverse-proxy pod IP, and there are >=2 such pods that round-robin. So consecutive failed logins for the same email alternate between identifiers like `10.232.132.143:x@y.com` and `10.232.131.130:x@y.com`, each getting its own counter that never hits 5. Verified by querying db.login_attempts after 7 failed logins for a single email: two rows, counts 5 and 1. Mitigation: change identifier to `email.lower()` (simplest) or parse X-Forwarded-For for the true client IP, and add a TTL index on login_attempts.locked_until.
